bd-melopsittacus-undulatus.title: Budgie (Parakeet)
bd-melopsittacus-undulatus.summary: The classic small pet parrot from the Australian grasslands. Budgies are playful, easy to hand-tame and among the best talkers of all parrots (males especially), and they come in many colors.
rows: About 7 in (18 cm) and 30–40 g; English show budgies are larger (about 8.5–9.5 in)
About 7–15 years with good care (many die younger from poor care)
A mix of quality seed with pellets, vegetables and fruit; an all-seed diet leads to tumors, goiter and other problems
Flock birds; enjoyable as a pair or group, or as a single bird that gets daily attention
Chatters and whistles; males are the best talkers and some learn hundreds of words
Drier inland grasslands and scrub of Australia

bd-psittacula-krameri.title: Indian Ringneck Parakeet
bd-psittacula-krameri.summary: A slim, long-tailed parakeet from India (and a separate population in tropical Africa), bred in many color mutations from green to blue, violet, grey and albino. Ringnecks are known for very clear speech, but they're vocal and active and need lots of room.
rows: About 16 in (40 cm) including the long tail; 116–140 g
At least 30 × 24 × 30 in (W × D × H) for one bird, bars no more than 1/2 in apart; much larger (an aviary) is better. Daily time out of the cage
Pellets made for medium parakeets as the base, with vegetables, greens, some fruit and a small seed mix as extras. Never chocolate, caffeine or avocado
Social and active; needs daily interaction and enrichment (chew toys, foot toys, ropes, swings, baths)
Very vocal, with shrieks and whistles; both sexes can learn to talk, often with very clear speech
Indian subcontinent and tropical northern Africa; feral populations in many countries
